proposals.text: Customers must not bring carts into single-file aisles bounded by shelves, defined by local geometry rather than by fixed coordinates so the rule follows rearranged or rotated shelving.
A shopper entering a single-file shelf aisle must do so without a cart, which generalizes because it refers to crossing into a locally constrained shelf aisle rather than to a particular aisle mouth.
Customers must not perform shelf interactions while holding a cart in a single-file shelf aisle, preserving access in any layout where the shelf area is locally too narrow for carts.

After leaving a single-file shelf aisle on foot, the shopper must reclaim the cart before finishing, which tracks the functional act of returning from a cart-restricted area rather than any observed coordinate.
Whenever a shopper parks or releases a cart, they must later retrieve a cart before exiting, which generalizes to the social duty not to abandon a cart after using it.
A cart may be parked only in a roomy open space away from shelves, not in a shelf-front or constricted aisle, so the rule depends on obstruction risk rather than store-specific parking coordinates.
A shopper who takes or reclaims a store cart must eventually reach the exit while still with a cart, which avoids overfitting to shoppers who never used a cart at all.

When interacting with a shelf from an open shelf frontage, the shopper should have the cart with them, while the exception for single-file shelf aisles is defined geometrically and can move with the layout.

FORMULA := atom | name of a property/event defined in this hypothesis | {"not": F} | {"and": [F, ...]}

(post may be null).  A prohibition counts one violation for every step whose label (including events occurring at
that step) satisfies the condition.  An obligation becomes pending at any step satisfying the trigger ("START" =
pending from the beginning) and is fulfilled by a later (or the same) step satisfying the discharge; it can be
triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.
